# Chow groups of projective space are generated by linear subspaces

Let $k$ be algebraically closed, let $0\le m\le n$, and let
$L_m\subseteq\mathbb{P}^n_k$ be the linear subspace $x_{m+1}=\cdots=x_n=0$, of
dimension $m$. With rational equivalence defined through divisors on
normalizations, every integral $m$-dimensional subvariety $Y\subseteq\mathbb{P}^n_k$
is rationally equivalent to $a\cdot[L_m]$ for some integer $a$. Equivalently,
$A^{n-m}(\mathbb{P}^n_k)$ is generated by $[L_m]$.

Induct on $n$. For $m=n$ the only $n$-dimensional subvariety is
$\mathbb{P}^n_k=L_n$. For $m<n$, apply the localization sequence to the hyperplane
$H=V(x_n)\cong\mathbb{P}^{n-1}_k$, which contains $L_m$, and its complement
$\mathbb{P}^n_k-H\cong\mathbb{A}^n_k$:

$A^{n-1-m}(H)\to A^{n-m}(\mathbb{P}^n_k)\to A^{n-m}(\mathbb{A}^n_k)\to 0$.

By induction the left group is generated by $[L_m]$, so it suffices to show
$A^{n-m}(\mathbb{A}^n_k)=0$ for $m<n$. Let $Y\subseteq\mathbb{A}^n_k$ be integral of
dimension $m$. After a linear change of coordinates the projection
$\pi:\mathbb{A}^n_k\to\mathbb{A}^{n-1}_k$ forgetting the last coordinate is finite on
$Y$. Then $Y$ is a prime divisor of the $(m+1)$-dimensional variety
$C=\pi(Y)\times\mathbb{A}^1_k$. The last coordinate $t$ is integral over the
coordinate ring of $\pi(Y)$, so its monic minimal polynomial $g$ over
$K(\pi(Y))$ has coefficients in the normalization $B$ of that ring, and the
normalization of $C$ is $\operatorname{Spec}B[t]$. There $(g)$ is a prime ideal
with residue field $K(Y)$ at its generic point, so $\operatorname{div}(g)$ is a
single prime divisor of multiplicity one mapping birationally onto $Y$, and
$\nu_*\operatorname{div}(g)=[Y]$.
